candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record describes a fluctuant mass spanning the palmar web space to the A2 pulley with an hourglass-shaped configuration bridging the superficial and deep palmar compartments — the hallmark anatomy of a collar button abscess. While flexor tenosynovitis can coexist and the focal tenderness over the flexor sheath and limited digit motion are noted, the primary diagnostic object is the collar button abscess (web space abscess with dumbbell extension). Pyogenic flexor tenosynovitis is a distinct entity defined by Kanavel's four cardinal signs and infection confined to the tendon sheath, not the web space. Asserting flexor tenosynovitis as the primary diagnosis conflicts with the anatomical scope of the reference diagnosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Flexor tenosynovitis is a related deep space infection of the hand but is anatomically and structurally distinct from a collar button abscess

case_quality_flags: Collar button abscess classic presentation: web space fluctuant mass with dumbbell extension through palmar fascia, diabetic host, traumatic inoculation without skin break
Flexor sheath tenderness may represent secondary involvement or early contiguous spread, not the primary diagnostic entity
